title_en: New ETFs to Watch: MANGOS, Tax Tricks and Boring Bitcoin
title_zh: 值得关注的新ETF：MANGOS、税务小技巧与'无聊'的比特币
subtitle_zh: 主持人 Joel Weber、Eric Balchunas 携手彭博新闻跨资产记者 Isabelle Lee，盘点三只值得关注的新ETF：借351条款递延资本利得税的 The Investment House ETF（TIH）、囊括 Meta、Anthropic、英伟达、谷歌/Alphabet、OpenAI 与 SpaceX 的 Yorkville America MANGOS Plus 指数ETF（代码 FRUT），以及一只'入场太晚'的对冲型比特币ETF（HBIT）。
summary_zh: 本期 Trillions'值得关注的新 ETF'环节，由 Joel Weber、Eric Balchunas 与 Bloomberg News 跨资产记者 Isabel Lee 一起盘点三只新品。'重头戏'是挂在白标服务商 ETF Architect 名下的 The Investment House ETF（代码 TIH），规模约 6 亿美元，本质是一次 351 条款转换（Section 351 exchange）：让持有大量浮盈的富豪把集中持股转入分散化 ETF，从而递延（而非免除）资本利得税——Balchunas 估算这类产品总规模已达约 170 亿美元，Lee 也提到 Melvin Capital 的 Gabe Plotkin 等家族都是玩家。第二只是 Yorkville America MANGOS Plus 指数 ETF（代码 FRUT），从'华丽七雄'（MAG7）延伸出'MANGOS'概念，囊括 Meta、Anthropic、Nvidia、Google/Alphabet、OpenAI 与 SpaceX 等 AI 巨头，其中 OpenAI 和 SpaceX 尚未上市、暂用占位符。第三只是对冲型比特币 ETF（HBIT），通过持有 IBIT 并用其期权对冲，费用率约 70 个基点；Balchunas 直言这类'对冲型'产品历来难做大，打赌它两年内撑不下去，更看好 NEOS 那种卖出深度虚值期权的'JEPI 式'收益产品。整体延续节目'淘遗珠'的轻松风格。

speakers.2: 播音员（Bloomberg Audio Studios 片头旁白）
speakers.3: Joel Weber（主持人，Trillions 联合主持）

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios.
turns.zh: 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）出品。

turns.en: Podcasts.
turns.zh: 播客。

turns.en: Radio. News. It's tough.
turns.zh: 广播。新闻。这活儿不好干。

turns.en: You know, it's tough to be that small trying to come in on something where you're like the sixth or seventh photonics. But I do like the name Aura.
turns.zh: 你知道，做一只这么小的基金，还想在一个你顶多算第六、第七名的光子学赛道里挤进去，真的很难。但我确实喜欢 Aura 这个名字。

turns.en: Why?
turns.zh: 为什么？

turns.en: Well, because my 15-year-old loves using that word all the time. I apparently have negative aura, but that's a whole other story.
turns.zh: 嗯，因为我家那个15岁的孩子天天挂在嘴边用这个词。据说我这人是'负气场（negative aura）'，不过那就是另外一个话题了。

turns.en: Welcome to Trillions. I'm Joel Weber.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Trillions。我是乔尔·韦伯（Joel Weber）。

turns.en: And I'm Eric Balchunas.
turns.zh: 我是埃里克·巴尔丘纳斯（Eric Balchunas）。

turns.en: Eric, you know what the world does not have enough of?
turns.zh: Eric，你知道这世上什么东西还不够多吗？

turns.en: Restaurants that have kiddie play centers.
turns.zh: 带儿童游乐区的餐厅。

turns.en: Not expecting that.
turns.zh: 这我可没想到。

turns.en: Isn't it crazy there's not more of those?
turns.zh: 你说离谱不离谱，这种餐厅怎么就这么少？

turns.en: They took them out.
turns.zh: 它们都被撤掉了。

turns.en: Chick-fil-A has one. That's why it's so popular.
turns.zh: Chick-fil-A（福乐鸡）就有一个，所以它才这么火。

turns.en: McDonald's used to have them. They don't have them anymore. Burger King, all gone.
turns.zh: 麦当劳以前有，现在没了。汉堡王，也全撤了。

turns.en: But yeah, need more of those.
turns.zh: 但是啊，这种餐厅确实该多来点。

turns.en: I was going to say exchange-traded funds.
turns.zh: 我本来想说'交易型开放式指数基金（ETF）'不够多。

turns.en: That too.
turns.zh: 那也算一个。

turns.en: There's thousands of them. Thousands.
turns.zh: 这类基金成千上万，成千上万只。

turns.en: No, there's too many, honestly.
turns.zh: 说实话，是太多了。

turns.en: But in August, there's been 128 new launches last month. We need more.
turns.zh: 但就说八月，上个月新发行了128只。我们还嫌不够。

turns.en: Yeah, there are six or seven launching a day this year. That's the pace we're at. It's mind-numbing. And I can't keep up with them. But yeah, it's pouring right now.
turns.zh: 是啊，今年一天就有六七只新发行，这就是现在的节奏。多到让人麻木，我根本跟不过来。但没错，现在简直就是'井喷'。

turns.en: But we're back with new ones to watch because there's always some gems out there. Yep. And joining us to walk through our three new ETFs to watch, Isabel Lee, cross-asset reporter at Bloomberg News. Welcome back, Isabel.
turns.zh: 不过我们又带着值得关注的新基金回来了，因为市面上总有那么几颗'遗珠'。是的。今天加入我们、一起过一遍这三只值得关注的新ETF的，是彭博新闻的跨资产记者伊莎贝尔·李（Isabelle Lee）。欢迎回来，Isabelle。

turns.en: Thank you. Excited to be here, as always.
turns.zh: 谢谢。一如既往，很高兴来到这里。

turns.en: This time on Trillions, new ETFs to watch. Okay, Eric, what's our big hit this episode?
turns.zh: 本期 Trillions，我们来聊聊值得关注的新ETF。好了，Eric，这一期的'重头戏'是哪只？

turns.en: So I just sort them by assets and I look, okay, what was the one with the most assets so far this month? And the answer is kind of a shocker, the investment house ETF, TIH. Never heard of it. It sounds like a one-off and I looked, it is under the white label ETF architect. So then I'm like, it's probably a 351 exchange.
turns.zh: 我就按资产规模排序，然后看，好，这个月到目前为止哪只资产最多？结果还挺出人意料——是 The Investment House ETF，代码 TIH。我从没听说过。它听起来像是一次性的产品，我查了一下，它挂在白标服务商 ETF Architect 名下。所以我就想，这多半是一次351条款转换（Section 351 exchange）。

turns.en: And it is.
turns.zh: 确实是。

turns.en: But it has, I believe, 600 million. That's a lot for a movie.
turns.zh: 但它据我了解有6亿美元的规模。对这么一次'操作'来说，这已经很多了。

turns.en: Reminder for people who don't know what a 351 conversion is.
turns.zh: 给不了解什么是351条款转换的听众解释一下。

turns.en: So if you have, let's say you have a stock or two and they've had so much gains and you just don't want to realize those gains now, there's a way to work with an ETF issuer to diversify your portfolio and move those stocks into a diversified ETF and defer your tax on that. And that way you can have... It's sort of like saying, hey, I have Navidi in this other stock and they're like really, really have a lot of gains and I don't want to realize them. So let me move them. I wish I had just like a Vanguard fund instead, but I don't want to sell those and buy Vanguard because it's a huge tax hit. So you can kind of merge those into a Vanguardian ETF and have a diversification and then defer your gains. You don't lose the basis that you bought it at. So you do pay, but you can defer. And there's been a couple of Bloomberg News articles on it. And there's a spectrum.
turns.zh: 这么说吧，假设你手上有一两只股票，它们涨了太多，你现在就是不想把这些浮盈落袋（实现利得）。这时有一种办法：你可以和一家ETF发行商合作，把投资组合分散化，把这些股票转入一只分散化的ETF，从而把相应的税负递延掉。这样一来你就……大概就是说，'嘿，我持有英伟达（Nvidia）还有另一只股票，它们真的、真的涨了一大截，我不想现在实现这些利得，那就让我把它们转出去吧。我真希望我当初持有的是一只先锋（Vanguard）基金，可我不想卖掉这些再去买Vanguard，因为那样税负太重。'于是你可以把这些股票'并入'一只类似Vanguard那样的ETF，实现分散化，同时递延你的利得。你并不会丢掉当初买入时的成本基础（basis），所以税你终究要交，但你可以递延。彭博新闻已经就这个主题写了好几篇报道，而且这类操作是分不同档次的。

turns.en: Much more popular.
turns.zh: 现在越来越流行了。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. There's a spirit of the law and they're pushing it a little. But this one looks pretty straightforward under ETF architect. And this is a growing business. I believe $ 17 billion worth of these.
turns.zh: 是啊是啊。法律有它的'立法精神'，而这些人有点在打擦边球。不过这一只看起来相当中规中矩，是在 ETF Architect 名下做的。而且这是一门正在壮大的生意，据我了解这类产品总规模已经有170亿美元了。

turns.en: We have written a lot about these stories and actually getting to the bottom of who is actually doing this, the families. It's becoming harder and harder, although some are out there. Like in our story, we wrote Melvin Capital. That's like, you know, the famous Gabe Plotkin, who we all knew him from the GameStop era and a.
turns.zh: 关于这类故事我们写过很多，而且真正去深挖背后到底是谁在做——是哪些家族——这件事正变得越来越难，尽管也有一些是公开的。比如在我们的一篇报道里，我们写了 Melvin Capital，也就是那位大名鼎鼎的加布·普洛特金（Gabe Plotkin），我们都是从那场 GameStop（游戏驿站）大战认识他的，还有……

turns.en: Lot of other rich families.
turns.zh: ……一大堆其他富豪家族。

turns.en: It's not illegal, but it's just to Eric's point, I think you just don't want to get any attention when it comes to lots of money and lots of taxes. And I looked into this ETF and they hold all the big tech companies that you can imagine. I mean, all of these tech bros out there, I think they're just so unimaginably rich. I'm sure you've seen this meme on Twitter or X now, Eric, like the SK Hynix or Samsung bros. They're just so darn rich now.
turns.zh: 这并不违法，但正如 Eric 说的，我觉得当涉及巨额财富和巨额税款时，你就是不想引来任何关注。我研究了这只ETF，它持有的都是你能想到的所有大型科技公司。我是说，外面这些科技大佬，我觉得他们简直富到难以想象。Eric，你肯定在推特（现在叫 X）上刷到过那个梗图，就是那帮'SK海力士（SK Hynix）兄弟'或者'三星（Samsung）兄弟'。他们现在真是太有钱了。

turns.en: Yeah, I think it's probably more of the older generation, I think, generally, because they have been in this market now for 20, 30 years. And they have a lot of gains and they hate taxes. And honestly, this move has been going on for a long time in the institutional world. Like if you're in the really, really rich bracket, you could just call up your banker, basically, and do a... You can convert your stock into what's called an exchange fund.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得总体上看，做这种操作的更多是老一代人，因为他们在这个市场里已经摸爬滚打了20年、30年，攒下了大量浮盈，而且他们痛恨交税。说实话，这种做法在机构圈子里已经存在很久了。比如，如果你属于那种超级富豪阶层，基本上你只要给你的银行家打个电话，就能……你可以把你的股票转换成一种叫'交换基金（exchange fund）'的东西。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: So this is just democratizing that move. Now, what's interesting is they actually open these up. So in a Schwab account, you can get in on these. So not all of them are done like bespoke. There's actually opening up to just regular people.
turns.zh: 所以现在做的，不过是把这种操作'平民化'了。有意思的是，他们真的把这些产品开放出来了。也就是说，在一个嘉信（Schwab）账户里，你就能买到这些。所以并不是所有这类产品都是定制的，它们其实正在向普通人敞开。

turns.en: Mm-hmm.
turns.zh: 嗯哼。

turns.en: Long story short, huge trend, kind of complex, but generally a tax story. So when you look at the holdings of this, it just looks like the S & P. It's nothing special. Nobody's bought it since this.
turns.zh: 长话短说，这是一大趋势，有点复杂，但归根到底是个税务故事。所以你看它的持仓，就跟标普（S&P）500差不多，没什么特别的。自那以后基本就没人再申购它了。

turns.en: I was going to ask. No. So the flows are like a one-time event effectively? Yeah.
turns.zh: 我正要问。不用了。所以资金流入实际上就等于一次性事件？是的。

turns.en: They're not launching this thinking, let's get all this money. So I was hesitant to pick it, but I thought it was a good time to talk about this because there's been a ton of news articles on it. And I was just at the ETF Architect had their annual event, which I speak at every other year. And it was a really good event. But I'd say a third of the sessions were on tax strategies. And the guy, Brett Sullivan, who's really known for this, he's a specialist, he was there talking about it. I mean, and his general message was, look, you have to be smart about this. And you have to adhere to some basic rules and principles. You can't go too hog wild. And I agree with that. I think ETF businesses, though, they like to push the envelope. So I think what now the Treasury may look at this And there may be a line drawn somewhere. I won't get into details, but it has to do with how many stocks you can come in with and how to diversify. There's like percentages.
turns.zh: 他们发行这只基金时，并不是想着'我们来把这笔钱都揽进来'。所以我一开始有点犹豫要不要选它，但我觉得现在正是聊这个话题的好时机，因为关于它的新闻报道已经铺天盖地了。我刚参加了 ETF Architect 的年度活动，我每隔一年就去那儿演讲一次，那是一场很不错的活动。但我得说，差不多有三分之一的环节都在讲税务策略。那位真正以此闻名、专门做这个的专家——布伦特·沙利文（Brent Sullivan）——也到场讲了。他的核心信息大致是：'看，这事你得做得聪明，你得遵守一些基本的规则和原则，不能太'放飞自我'。'我认同这点。不过我觉得ETF这行的人喜欢'把信封撑到极限'（游走在边缘）。所以现在财政部（Treasury）可能会来审视这件事，也许会在某个地方划一条线。细节我就不展开了，但它跟你能带多少只股票进来、以及如何分散化有关，里面有一些百分比的讲究。

turns.en: Because I'm the house now, says Scott Besson.
turns.zh: 因为'我现在就是庄家（the house）'——这是斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）说的。

turns.en: You are the house now.
turns.zh: 你现在就是庄家。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: I'm the house now. You don't want to cross the house, man.
turns.zh: '我现在就是庄家。'你可别去得罪庄家，兄弟。

turns.en: I am the law.
turns.zh: '我就是法律。'

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: That's what that reminds me of.
turns.zh: 这正是它让我联想到的。

turns.en: I'm the captain now. Yeah.
turns.zh: '我现在就是船长。'对。

turns.en: I'm the captain.
turns.zh: '我就是船长。'

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好吧。

turns.en: So if I have the money and I want to do one of these 351 conversions and someone creates this ETF for me, what are– How much are they charging in the basis points in this ETF?
turns.zh: 那假如我有这笔钱，想做一次这样的351条款转换，有人替我创设了这只ETF，那么——他们在这只ETF里收多少费用？以基点（basis points）计是多少？

turns.en: Like, is there a silver lining in this ETF, which is that maybe it's cheap?
turns.zh: 比如说，这只ETF里有没有什么'一线曙光'，也就是它也许很便宜？

turns.en: It's 100 basis points, Joel. So I'm not sure if you'd want to do that. It's kind of pricey for... Is it.
turns.zh: 费率是100个基点，Joel。所以我不确定你会不会想这么做。对……来说这有点贵。

turns.en: Pricey, Eric?
turns.zh: 贵吗，Eric？

turns.en: I don't totally understand the high fee, to be honest with you. So that... And if you look at the.
turns.zh: 说实话，我并不能完全理解这个高费率。所以……而且如果你看看它的……

turns.en: Maybe it's the moat.
turns.zh: 也许这就是它的'护城河'吧。

turns.en: If you look at the stocks, I mean, you can get that for three bips now, too.
turns.zh: 如果你看它持有的那些股票，我是说，现在你只花三个基点也能买到同样的东西。

turns.en: So I.
turns.zh: 所以我……

turns.en: This is not about a product that they're trying to get investors into, I don't think. However, I've seen bespoke products come in. There's one that was recently put out that CalPERS seeded with State Street. And a lot of times those are pretty low cost because I think State Street's like, look, we have this anchor tenant. Let's make it lower fee and competitive just in case other people want to come in. This one just doesn't seem like it cares, which is fine. There's a group of people who convert separate accounts. ETFs are just so damn benefit rich that people convert a lot of things into them. And not everybody cares about getting new investors. Most of them do. This is just an example of one that doesn't. But yeah, that It's a new world. You know, normally I would go to the top of the list and see like a BlackRock or Vanguard ETF. And now you never know what you're going to see up there.
turns.zh: 我觉得这并不是一只他们想方设法要把投资者拉进来的产品。不过，我确实见过一些定制型产品进场。最近就有一只，是加州公务员退休基金（CalPERS）与道富（State Street）合作'播种'（seed）设立的。很多时候这类产品成本相当低，因为我想道富的心态是：'看，我们有了这个'锚定租户'，那我们就把费率定低一点、更有竞争力一点，万一还有别人想进来呢。'而这一只看起来就是压根不在乎，这也没关系。有一群人会把独立账户（separate account）转换过来。ETF的好处实在是太'富集'了，以至于人们把很多东西都转换成ETF。而且并不是每个人都在乎吸引新投资者——大多数在乎，这只是一个不在乎的例子。但没错，这是一个新世界。你知道，通常我打开榜单最上面看到的，会是贝莱德（BlackRock）或者先锋（Vanguard）的ETF。而现在，你永远不知道榜首会冒出来个什么东西。

turns.en: I'm glad you picked this because, again, it shows that asset managers are increasingly using tax efficient packages and ETF is one of them. And you got into a healthy debate on X about this. And I saw it, that it's tax deferral. It's not really like you're never going to pay taxes anymore. And I think that's the important thing that people just need to remember.
turns.zh: 我很高兴你选了这只，因为这再次说明，资产管理公司越来越多地在使用'税务高效'的包装，而ETF就是其中一种。你还为这个在 X 上引发了一场挺健康的辩论，我看到了——关键是它是'税负递延'，并不是说你从此就再也不用交税了。我觉得这才是大家真正需要记住的重点。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: I mean, the headline will say DODGE. you know, from Bloomberg. And I understand you could do mental gymnastics and say it is a dodge and it, well, you'll get more clicks, which I can understand. I try to get clicks too.
turns.zh: 我是说，彭博的标题会写'避税（DODGE）'。我理解你可以做一番'脑力体操'，非说这就是'躲避'，而且这样能拿到更多点击量，这我能理解，我也想多要点击量。

turns.en: Don't worry.
turns.zh: 别担心。

turns.en: But I think defer, you know, you put deferment in a defer deferment in a headline.
turns.zh: 但我觉得该用'递延（defer）'，你把'递延'放进标题里……

turns.en: I'm sorry.
turns.zh: 抱歉。

turns.en: It's just like investor repellent. It's like, that's so boring of a word anyway. Believe me, I know. Cause I put institutional in the name of a book and like, it was like spring reader repellent on the title. And so deferment is sort of like that, but dodge is like a little more like, ooh, what's going on here? So I get it. But in the story, they say it's deferment. And that's what the industry would push back on. However, you could say, well, the government really should have that money now. Then they can do other things with it. Whereas you defer, you're starving the government of money and you can actually invest it and make more money. So therefore, I looked at the word dodge and it means to avoid completely. So I just think definitionally defer is more accurate.
turns.zh: ……那简直就是'投资者驱避剂'。反正'递延'这个词也太无聊了。相信我，我懂，因为我曾经在一本书的书名里放了'机构（institutional）'这个词，结果那标题活脱脱就是'读者驱避剂'。所以'递延'差不多就是那种感觉，而'避税（dodge）'就更像'哦？这里面有什么猫腻？'所以我理解他们为什么这么用。但在报道正文里，他们说的是'递延'，而这正是业界会反驳的地方。不过你也可以说，政府其实现在就该拿到那笔钱，然后拿去做别的事；而你一递延，就等于让政府'断了粮'，你自己却能拿这笔钱去投资、去赚更多的钱。因此我查了'dodge'这个词，它的意思是'完全避开'。所以单从定义上讲，我觉得'defer（递延）'更准确。

turns.en: Thank you for that GRE lesson, Eric.
turns.zh: 谢谢你给我们上的这堂 GRE（美国研究生入学考试）词汇课，Eric。

turns.en: Okay, I'm curious how you're going to follow that since that was a little bit of a wild card. What's our actual wild card ETF for this episode? All right, you ready for this one? Yeah.
turns.zh: 好吧，我很好奇你接下来要怎么接，因为刚才那段算是个小小的'神来之笔'。那我们这一期真正的'外卡（wild card）'ETF是哪只？好，你准备好听这只了吗？

turns.en: I'm going to drop a new Wall Street acronym on you. You know the MAG7?
turns.zh: 我要给你们抛一个华尔街的新缩写。你们知道'华丽七雄（MAG7）'吧？

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 知道。

turns.en: Get ready for mangoes, okay? The Yorkville America Mangoes Plus Index ETF, ticker FRUT, F-R-U-T.
turns.zh: 准备好迎接'芒果（MANGOS）'吧。它是 Yorkville America MANGOS Plus 指数ETF，代码 FRUT，F-R-U-T。

turns.en: The ticker is the winner for me, although we've seen a lot of filings about mangoes.
turns.zh: 对我来说，光是这个代码就已经赢麻了，尽管我们已经看到一大堆关于'芒果'的备案申请。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊是啊。

turns.en: I don't think they invented Mango.
turns.zh: 我倒不觉得'Mango'这个词是他们发明的。

turns.en: What does Mango mean again?
turns.zh: 'Mango'到底是什么意思来着？

turns.en: Mango stands for Meta, Anthropic, NVIDIA, Google slash Alphabet, OpenAI, and SpaceX. And I think the noteworthy thing there is that there are two companies there that are private.
turns.zh: Mango 代表 Meta、Anthropic、英伟达（NVIDIA）、谷歌/Alphabet（Google/Alphabet）、OpenAI 和 SpaceX。我觉得值得注意的一点是，这里面有两家是未上市（私营）公司。

turns.en: So again, this is a story of.
turns.zh: 所以你看，这又是一个关于……的故事。

turns.en: But going public, we think.
turns.zh: ……是关于它们要上市的故事，我们这么认为。

turns.en: Yes, we think. Our reporting says soon. But again, if this just.
turns.zh: 是的，我们这么认为。我们的报道说'快了'。但话说回来，如果这只基金……

turns.en: talks to us about putting private assets in an ETF, how that will work. Is it going to be in an SPV or do they have a cap table exposure and all that? But yes, mangoes is a new thing. I was trying to make an index of it to compare it with MAG7. And I was like, oh my gosh, you're so silly. Again, two companies are so private.
turns.zh: ……它正好跟我们谈到了'如何把私营资产装进一只ETF'，这会怎么运作。是通过一个特殊目的载体（SPV）来持有，还是他们拿到了股权架构表（cap table）上的敞口，诸如此类？但没错，'芒果（MANGOS）'是个新事物。我本来还想给它做一个指数，好和 MAG7 做对比，然后我就想，'天呐，你也太傻了'——因为其中有两家可是彻头彻尾的私营公司。

turns.en: Yeah, and it does hold, there was a leveraged mangoes that came out, but it doesn't hold those two privates. And so they actually lower cased.
turns.zh: 是啊，而且它确实持有——之前出过一只加杠杆的'芒果'，但它并不持有那两家私营公司。所以他们实际上把名字做成了'小写版'。

turns.en: No, stop.
turns.zh: 别，打住。

turns.en: Really?
turns.zh: 真的假的？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: This is too much.
turns.zh: 这也太过了。

turns.en: Yeah, this is too much. Anyway, this one is legit, though, because now it does hold the OpenAI and Anthropic through special purpose vehicles. But it's pretty much all you can do unless you have a connection. And this one actually, the plus.
turns.zh: 是啊，这也太过了。不管怎样，这一只倒是'货真价实'，因为它现在确实通过特殊目的载体持有了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。但除非你有人脉，否则这基本上就是你能做到的极限了。而这一只其实，那个'Plus'……

turns.en: But those must be placeholders, too. Like, wait until they go public and then.
turns.zh: 不过那些肯定也只是'占位符'。就是，等它们上市了，然后就……

turns.en: It'll be replaced.
turns.zh: 就会被替换掉。

turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: And then when they go public, those two companies, then what makes this special? It's just going to be like any other.
turns.zh: 那等这两家公司上市之后，这只基金还有什么特别之处呢？它不就变得和其他任何一只一样了嘛。

turns.en: Well, AI is not going away.
turns.zh: 嗯，人工智能（AI）可不会消失。

turns.en: I guess so.
turns.zh: 我想也是。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: But anthropic, I mean, some of the debates around anthropic and like how these AI is going to like destroy the human race. This is heavy duty stuff. So I think for an investor, like I know when I travel around and talk to like regular investors, they really want to get into AI. They think it's going to be big. So even if it holds it after it goes public, Maybe there's a downturn because there's like SpaceX, you know, it goes public and then people sell it. Over time, I just think like, is open AI and anthropic really going to go away? I mean, this is a big trend. They also have a plus on there and they own what's called the Parabolic 7. What is that? This reminds me of the Western movies of like the 50s, like the Magnificent 7 and like the Hardcore 8, whatever.
turns.zh: 但说到 Anthropic，我是说，围绕 Anthropic 的一些争论，比如这些AI会怎么'毁灭人类'之类的——这可是相当'硬核'的东西。所以我觉得对投资者来说，我知道我到处跑、跟普通投资者聊的时候，他们是真的很想上车AI，觉得这会是个大趋势。所以哪怕它是在这些公司上市之后才持有，也许中间会有一波下跌，因为比如 SpaceX 上市后大家会抛售。但把时间拉长看，我就是想：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 真的会消失吗？我是说，这是一股大趋势。它名字里还有个'Plus'，而且它持有所谓的'抛物线七雄（Parabolic 7）'。那又是什么？这让我想起上世纪50年代的那些西部片，比如《豪勇七蛟龙》（The Magnificent Seven），还有什么'硬汉八人组'之类的。

turns.en: Okay, anyway.
turns.zh: 好吧，总之。

turns.en: No one remembers.
turns.zh: 没人记得那些了。

turns.en: The Parabolic 7. SanDisk, Marvel, Micron, Intel, Dell, AMD, and Broadcom.
turns.zh: '抛物线七雄'是：闪迪（SanDisk）、迈威尔（Marvell）、美光（Micron）、英特尔（Intel）、戴尔（Dell）、AMD 和博通（Broadcom）。

turns.en: Oh, so it's like the support network.
turns.zh: 哦，所以它就像那个'后援网络'。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So, I mean, these are some hot, highfalutin stocks here, Joel. So, look, I could see this maybe gaining attraction. Like, this is the kind of ETF that could go on a run. Now, whether it, like, takes over from the Mag7 and Mangos becomes, like, a household word, I don't know. I have not heard it outside of these ETF filings. Like, no one's running around saying, like, Mangos this, Mango that. Whereas Mag 7 is definitely in like the vernacular.
turns.zh: 所以说，Joel，这里头可都是一些火爆、'高大上'的股票。你看，我能想象这只也许会'受到追捧'（gaining traction）。这就是那种有可能'一飞冲天'的ETF。至于它能不能从 MAG7 手里'接棒'、让'芒果（MANGOS）'变成一个家喻户晓的词，我就不知道了。除了这些ETF备案文件之外，我没在别处听到过它。就是，没人在外面张口'芒果'、闭口'芒果'地喊。而 MAG7 绝对已经进入'日常口语'了。

turns.en: It's still early.
turns.zh: 现在还早。

turns.en: It's still early.
turns.zh: 现在还早。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: But anyway.
turns.zh: 但总之。

turns.en: People are talking about mangoes though. Yeah. A thing I did not know. There are hundreds of species of mangoes. Did you know that?
turns.zh: 不过大家确实在聊'芒果'。是啊。有件事我以前不知道：芒果有几百个品种。你知道吗？

turns.en: Of course. And the Philippines has the best mangoes.
turns.zh: 当然知道。而且菲律宾的芒果最好吃。

turns.en: So it makes sense. The metaphor.
turns.zh: 所以这个比喻还挺说得通。

turns.en: I think India is going to dispute that.
turns.zh: 我觉得印度会对此提出异议。

turns.en: My husband actually who is Indian. This is the biggest debate in our home.
turns.zh: 我先生正好是印度人。这是我们家里最大的一场争论。

turns.en: He says his are better. Of course. No, no.
turns.zh: 他会说他的（印度芒果）更好吃。当然。不不。

turns.en: How about the other debate? We have the cleaning people come sometimes. And then because we always talk about. My wife is insane the day before they come. She like cleans the whole house. And if I have anything lying around, she's like, clean it up. And I'm like, well, what's the point of having the people come then?
turns.zh: 那再说说另一场争论吧？我们有时会请保洁上门。然后因为我们总是聊到这个——我太太在保洁来的前一天简直'疯魔'，她会把整个房子打扫一遍。我要是有任何东西乱放，她就说'给我收拾干净'。我就想，那还请保洁来干嘛呢？

turns.en: This is called the pre-clean. Yeah.
turns.zh: 这叫'预清洁（pre-clean）'。是啊。

turns.en: Of course.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: You always have to clean before the kind cleaning lady comes.
turns.zh: 你总得在那位好心的保洁阿姨来之前先打扫一遍。

turns.en: So the kind cleaning lady doesn't think you're messy.
turns.zh: 好让那位好心的保洁阿姨觉得你不是个邋遢鬼。

turns.en: That's the thing. It's about the image that she's portraying. And I'm like, oh my God. The day before the cleaners come is always like.
turns.zh: 问题就在这儿。这关乎她要塑造出来的'形象'。我就想，天呐。保洁来的前一天永远是这样……

turns.en: It's not the day. It's the five minutes.
turns.zh: 不是'前一天'，是'那五分钟'。

turns.en: Wait, do you do that?
turns.zh: 等等，你也会这么干？

turns.en: My wife's way prior planning.
turns.zh: 我太太是提前很久就规划好的那种。

turns.en: I shove everything in a closet or the laundry hamper and I'm like, take it as it is. But it's a thing.
turns.zh: 我是把所有东西一股脑塞进壁橱或者洗衣篮里，然后心想'就这样吧，爱咋咋地'。但这确实是个普遍现象。

turns.en: No, we clean because we don't want to.
turns.zh: 不，我们打扫是因为我们不想……

turns.en: We don't clean.
turns.zh: 我们才不打扫呢。

turns.en: We just like sort.
turns.zh: 我们只是稍微'归置'一下。

turns.en: We don't want the cleaners to think that this client is the messiest.
turns.zh: 我们是不想让保洁觉得，这家客户是最邋遢的那一个。

turns.en: We want to be the best.
turns.zh: 我们想做最棒的那一个。

turns.en: I know. It's a very.
turns.zh: 我知道。这真的很……

turns.en: I'm with your wife on this one, Eric.
turns.zh: 这件事上我站你太太，Eric。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: So how many Mango ETFs are we going to see?
turns.zh: 那我们会看到多少只'芒果（Mango）'ETF？

turns.en: So I think we have a couple on the market. I think we're going to see probably like six or seven. And then we'll see if they take off. If they do, we'll see way more. But I know Corgi.
turns.zh: 我觉得市面上已经有那么几只了。我估计我们大概会看到六到七只。然后就看它们能不能'起飞'。如果能，那我们会看到多得多的。不过我知道 Corgi……

turns.en: Of course, they have one.
turns.zh: 当然，他们也有一只。

turns.en: They have everything. Corgi has one.
turns.zh: 他们什么都有。Corgi 就有一只。

turns.en: Only one?
turns.zh: 只有一只？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: We'll see.
turns.zh: 我们走着瞧。

turns.en: There might be two. They probably have a leverage too. I can't remember, but I know they have one at least straight up one. But the Yorkville one I'm tracking because it does have the privates in there.
turns.zh: 可能有两只。他们大概也有一只加杠杆的。我记不清了，但我知道他们至少有一只'纯多头'的。不过我一直在盯 Yorkville 那一只，因为它确实把那几家私营公司装进去了。

turns.en: And what was the ticker? Fruit. F-R-U-T.
turns.zh: 代码是什么来着？FRUT（'水果'）。F-R-U-T。

turns.en: Good ticker.
turns.zh: 好代码。

turns.en: It starts with 50 basis points, right?
turns.zh: 它起步费率是50个基点，对吧？

turns.en: 50 bips. Not bad. I mean, it's reasonable for a hot saucy type product.
turns.zh: 50个基点。不错。对一款'热辣型'的产品来说，这算合理的。

turns.en: All right. Final category. Love this one in general. Good luck with that. Who's our winner? All right.
turns.zh: 好。最后一个类别。我一般都很爱这个环节——'祝你好运吧（Good luck with that）'。我们这期的'胜出者'是谁？好。

turns.en: Good luck with that this week. Before I get to my real pick, there's one that just caught my attention. I just got to go over it. The Aura AI Photonics ETF, P-H-O-X. It's tough. It's tough to be that small trying to come in on something where you're like the sixth or seventh photonics. But I do like the name Aura.
turns.zh: 本周的'祝你好运吧'。在讲我真正的'心头好'之前，有一只刚刚抓住了我的注意力，我得先说一说：Aura AI 光子学ETF，代码 P-H-O-X。这很难。做一只这么小的基金，还想在一个你顶多算第六、第七名的光子学赛道里挤进去，真的很难。但我确实喜欢 Aura 这个名字。

turns.en: Why?
turns.zh: 为什么？

turns.en: Well, because my 15-year-old Loves using that word all the time. I apparently have negative aura, but that's a whole nother story.
turns.zh: 嗯，因为我家那个15岁的孩子天天挂在嘴边用这个词。据说我这人是'负气场'，不过那就是另外一个话题了。

turns.en: Your wife will also say that the day the cleaner comes.
turns.zh: 你太太在保洁上门那天也会这么说你。

turns.en: He went to camp two years ago and him and his friend were like, this one counselor has like aura to give. He was like, so cool. This guy was so cool. He's like, he has aura to give. Anyway, aura is like the new word. Do you have permanently negative.
turns.zh: 他两年前去参加夏令营，他和朋友就说，某个辅导员'气场（aura）爆表'。他说'太酷了，这人太酷了，他气场满到能分给别人'。总之，'aura'就是那个新词。（他们会问）你是永久性的负气场……

turns.en: Aura or day to day you have different auras?
turns.zh: ……还是说你每天的气场都不一样？

turns.en: No. To his kid, it's permanent.
turns.zh: 不。对他的孩子来说，这是'永久'的。

turns.en: Yeah. For my kid, it's negative permanent aura. Anyway, I like the name. It's kind of like speaks to Gen Z. Yeah. But it's really tough. And the ticker is P-H-O-X. That wasn't even my real pick, Joel. The real pick, yeah. I just wanted to talk Aura for a minute. I'm obsessed with these words that my kid uses. Aura is probably a top fiver.
turns.zh: 是啊。对我的孩子来说，我就是永久性的负气场。不管怎样，我喜欢这个名字，它有点'对Z世代（Gen Z）的胃口'。是啊。但这只基金真的很难做。而且代码是 P-H-O-X。这其实还不是我真正的'心头好'，Joel。真正的那只——对——我只是想先聊聊 Aura。我特别着迷于我家孩子用的这些词，'aura'大概能排进前五。

turns.en: But OK, what was the real one?
turns.zh: 那好吧，你真正的那只是哪个？

turns.en: Yeah. The real one is the Hedgeye Hedged Bitcoin ETF HBIT. The reason I picked this one is because it's, again, very late in the Bitcoin launching, number one. Number two, hedged. Bitcoin, I think, is a hot sauce. And I think that when you have a portfolio, most people who use ETFs are going to have just a little Bitcoin. They don't want to hedge. They don't want any part of that. They want to experience the pure melt-up. Bitcoin went up like 25% or something in like a couple weeks. When it moves, it moves quick. And so a lot of the buffers and the hedging ones just don't take off anyway. And if you're late, it's definitely not It's going to be tough.
turns.zh: 真正的那只是 Hedgeye 对冲比特币ETF，代码 HBIT。我选它的原因是：第一，它在比特币产品里入场已经非常晚了；第二，'对冲型'比特币，我觉得是个'热辣'的卖点。我觉得当你构建一个投资组合时，大多数用ETF的人只会配一点点比特币，他们不想对冲，一点都不想沾那个，他们想体验的是纯粹的'暴涨（melt-up）'。比特币曾经在几周里涨了大概25%之类的。它一旦动起来，就动得飞快。所以很多'缓冲型'和'对冲型'产品本来就走不起来。而如果你入场又晚，那它就肯定——会很难。

turns.en: There was a moment, though, where hedge currency ETFs were a thing. Is there something to read into this because of that?
turns.zh: 不过曾经有那么一阵子，'对冲货币型ETF'是很火的东西。就因为那段历史，这件事是不是也有值得琢磨的地方？

turns.en: No, I don't think so. Because when Bitcoin went down after that run up, it went down like 1.3% since this launched. And this one, I think it saved you 30 bps. It just wasn't a lot of buffer. And so I think the idea here is instead of being like a permanent buffer where we're always hedged, we're going to actually have dynamic hedge. So we can actually look at market signals. HedgeEyes, you know, definitely looks at signals and they have a couple of the products I think are more appropriate for signals. I just think when it comes to Bitcoin, people don't- You want it all. You want it pure.
turns.zh: 不，我不这么认为。因为比特币在那波上涨之后回落，自这只基金成立以来其实只跌了大约1.3%，而它我觉得帮你省下了30个基点，根本起不到多少'缓冲'作用。所以我觉得这里的思路是：与其做一个'我们永远都在对冲'的永久性缓冲，不如做一个动态对冲，这样就能真正去观察市场信号。Hedgeye 你懂的，绝对是看信号的，而且他们有几只产品我觉得更适合用信号来驱动。我只是觉得，一说到比特币，人们不想要别的——你要的是全部，你要的是纯粹。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: And I think it's, and again, it's a little late and Bitcoin's already really got its face ripped off. Like maybe if this was launched before the face ripper, but now I think people are like, if they're going to buy it, they're like, they want the upswing now. They don't want to hedge.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得，再说一次，它入场有点晚，而比特币已经被砸得'鼻青脸肿'了。也许如果它是在那波'血洗'之前推出的话……但现在我觉得，人们如果打算买，他们想要的是'上涨行情'，他们不想对冲。

turns.en: So Maybe. We'll see.
turns.zh: 所以，也许吧。我们走着瞧。

turns.en: I'll eat my words if this thing gets asset. But if I had to bet, this thing won't be around.
turns.zh: 如果这东西真能吸引到资产，我就收回我的话、认打认罚。但要我打赌的话，这东西撑不下去。

turns.en: In two years.
turns.zh: 两年之内。

turns.en: Why do you think they are holding Bitcoin ETPs, ETFs, rather than just Bitcoin directly? That's like Joel said, meta, earlier.
turns.zh: 你觉得他们为什么持有比特币ETP、比特币ETF，而不是直接持有比特币呢？就像 Joel 之前说的，这有点'meta'（自指）。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Well, for a lot of hedge fund type places, and if you're not really wanting to take on a lot of exposure, the ETF is just easier. I mean, I bet, to be honest with you, even a professional investor who goes to like a Bitcoin exchange, you'd get a better price just trading iBit at a one or two basis point spread. You do have to pay the management fee per year, but that's only like 20 something basis points. It's honestly a better deal than going direct.
turns.zh: 嗯，对很多对冲基金类型的机构来说，如果你并不真想承担太多敞口，那么ETF就是更省事的选择。我是说，说句实话我打赌，即便是那种会去比特币交易所的专业投资者，你直接交易 IBIT、只付一到两个基点的买卖价差，反而能拿到更好的价格。你确实得每年付管理费，但那也只有二十几个基点而已。老实说，这比直接买比特币还划算。

turns.en: This ETF, I think the expense ratio is 70 BIPs. I just don't know. I feel like people who invest in Bitcoin want it for the volatility and now you want more in Bitcoin.
turns.zh: 这只ETF，我记得费用率是70个基点。我也说不好。我就是觉得，投资比特币的人图的就是它的波动性，而现在你却想给他们多一点'比特币之外的东西'。

turns.en: Yeah, I think it's the bigger. I don't think people would judge this one for owning iBit. I think Because they're not reselling iBit. They're not saying, yeah, that would be weird. But they're just like, look, we're going to use iBit. And they probably use iBit options to hedge when they want to. And those are very liquid and cheap markets. I think that's a smart move, honestly, versus using Bitcoin directly. I just think this is one of those categories that I just don't ever see any of these hedging products really doing much. The only one I could see maybe taking off is the JEPI one, like where you take Bitcoin and you go way out of the money. So you do get like, I would say 80% of Bitcoin's upside. You give a little bit and you sell that to get some income. So that company Goldman bought Neos, they have a Bitcoin premium income ETF. And so if you're looking for income and you're like a boomer, you can use Bitcoin's volatility to get more income. That's a different situation. I think those can be mildly successful. And I've seen these hedge ETFs that are dynamic. It is so hard to time the market over and over. You might get it once, but they're very difficult. So equity hedge ETFs haven't sold really that well either.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得这是更大的问题。我不觉得人们会因为这只基金持有 IBIT 就'看轻'它，因为他们并不是在'转售' IBIT——他们不是那种'来，买我的 IBIT'，那样确实会很怪。他们的心态是'看，我们就要用 IBIT'，而且他们很可能在需要对冲时用 IBIT 期权来对冲，而那些是非常有流动性、也非常便宜的市场。老实说，我觉得相比直接用比特币，这是聪明的一招。我只是觉得，这类产品属于那种我从来没见过哪个'对冲型'产品能真正做起来的大类。唯一我能想象也许会走红的，是那种'JEPI 式'的——就是你拿着比特币，卖出深度虚值（way out of the money）的期权。这样你仍然能拿到，我会说，比特币大约80%的上涨空间，你让渡一点点，靠卖出期权换取一些收益。所以像那家被高盛（Goldman）收购的公司 NEOS，他们就有一只比特币溢价收益ETF。因此如果你在找收益、又是个'婴儿潮一代（boomer）'，你可以利用比特币的波动性去获取更多收益。那是另一种情形，我觉得这类产品能取得'温和'的成功。我也见过那种动态的对冲ETF——一次又一次地精准择时实在太难了。你也许能蒙对一次，但它们非常难做。所以股票类对冲ETF的销量其实也一直不太好。

turns.en: So good luck with that.
turns.zh: 所以，'祝你好运吧'。

turns.en: Yeah. Isabel, thanks for joining us on Trillions.
turns.zh: 是啊。Isabelle，感谢做客 Trillions。

turns.en: Always a pleasure.
turns.zh: 一如既往，荣幸之至。
